text: {"frames":["Jaap the dream seller grabbed the frame of the portrait just as the painted lady turned her head toward the stairs. Fresh paint still wet on her cheek, she was already stepping out of the canvas. Behind her hangs a clock on the corridor wall, painted with the same careful brush, and its hands point at a clear time. \"Hold the rope, quick,\" he shouted, and the knot slipped against the wood. What time does the clock in the picture show? Write the time with digits.","Imogen the old lock keeper pushed her shoulder against the sluice gate, because the water in the chamber was rising and falling like a sleeping cat's chest. Her neighbour Hendrik was already shouting from the far bank that he wanted the lock open before the ice bell rang. Above the lock house a clock hangs in the picture, its face yellow with age, and its hands are the only thing in the room that agrees with anyone. Imogen squinted at it and sighed. What time does the clock in the picture show? Write the time with digits.","The smell of burnt waffles came up from the stairs that were not on the plan, and Sanne the cheese maker followed it with her wooden clog in one hand. The landing at the top was empty except for a small painted clock on the wall, the kind a mill keeper would hang above the flour bins. Its hands were stuck in a way that made the mill wheel below creak as if it were holding its breath. Sanne made a bet with herself that the clock was telling the truth. What time does the clock in the picture show? Write the time with digits.","A blue lantern bobbed across the barge deck with nobody holding it, and Fenna the learned owl swivelled her head to watch it go. She had read every book in the mill library and knew a lantern does not light itself without a reason. Beside the mast hangs a clock in the picture, its glass cracked along one edge but its hands still moving. Fenna tapped her beak twice against the rail and waited for the answer. What time does the clock in the picture show? Write the time with digits.","The canal had run backwards all night, and Briony the talking stork stood on the wrong bank, shaking the water from her feathers and complaining loudly. The tulip boats had drifted up the slope and the millers were arguing about it on the dyke. High on the windmill wall a clock is painted in the picture, and Briony swore it had been ticking the other way round since sunset. She tilted her head and squinted at the hands. What time does the clock in the picture show? Write the time with digits."]}
